result: In 144 women with post-COVID fatigue (78 meeting CCC), repeated handgrip strength was similarly impaired in PCS and ME/CFS but correlated with PEM, fatigue, cognition and autonomic symptoms only in ME/CFS.

result: In 270 long COVID patients from Jena and Oxford, simple reaction time was about 3 SD slower than healthy controls, 53.5% were more than 2 SD slower, the effect replicated across both clinics, was not explained by fatigue, depression, anxiety, sleep or PTSD, and correlated with sustained-attention deficits.
reason: Long COVID population, not an ME/CFS replication; adds a long COVID version of the reaction-time deficit

result: In 169 long COVID patients, mean peak VO2 was 24.4 mL/kg/min with 36% below predicted and 54% with a low VO2/workload slope; in 41 retested at 1 year no CPET parameter changed.
reason: Uncontrolled retrospective case series compared with predicted values, not recovered controls; adds 1-year time course showing no improvement

result: In a prospective post-mononucleosis student cohort, modified Beighton scores did not differ significantly between 53 who developed ME/CFS at 6 months and 66 recovered controls; females scored higher than males.
reason: Same measure (Beighton score) tested prospectively with a null result

result: Among 25 young people with ME/CFS after EBV mononucleosis (12 adolescents, 13 young adults), 6/12 adolescents no longer met criteria at 12 months while all young adults still met CCC; median time to diagnosis was 13.8 months.
reason: Follows established post-IM ME/CFS cases rather than an IM cohort, so not a replication of incidence rates; adds an adolescent vs young-adult prognosis difference

result: In 25 young people with post-EBV ME/CFS, EBV serology and EBV DNA load did not correlate with clinical features and clinical chemistry showed no inflammation.
reason: No control group; it tests within-patient correlation with symptoms, not patient vs control seroprevalence

result: In 351 patients hospitalised with COVID-19 vs 2,927 normative controls, one-year global cognitive deficits were associated with elevated serum brain injury markers and reduced anterior cingulate volume, with acute corticosteroids appearing protective.
reason: Population is post-hospitalisation moderate-to-severe COVID with encephalopathy, not ME/CFS or long COVID fatigue; elevated injury markers there do not test the ME/CFS null claim

result: In 351 patients hospitalised with COVID-19, cognitive deficits at one year were global, scaled with acute illness severity and encephalopathy, and matched subjective complaints.
reason: Shows deficits so 'contradicts' is wrong, and the population is post-hospitalisation brain injury rather than ME/CFS; no fitting finding

result: When ME/CFS patients were stratified by immune competence, those without immunodeficiency had elevated lipopolysaccharide-binding protein (mucosal barrier leakage), while immunodeficient patients had reduced complement C4a.
reason: Same marker (LBP) by ELISA; adds an immune-competence subgroup; not the cited Rohrhofer 2025 Allergy paper
